newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Record stocks weigh on mogas.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Record stocks weigh on mogas.

text.p: Gasoline prices slumped on Thursday under the pressure of weaker crudes and record high stocks in Singapore.
Singapore light distillates stocks rose to a record 7.603 million barrels for the week ending April 16, up another 366,000 barrels, Singapore's Trade Development Board figures showed.
Light distillates stocks have been rising steadily since the week ending March 12 and is now at a two-year high.
Although light distillates stocks comprise gasoline, reformate and naphtha, traders said the barrels were mainly gasoline.
"I don't take notice of the figures,' said a trader. "It is old news that it is chock-full."
Early May fob Singapore barrels extended their losses with the 95-octane unleaded grade offered at $24.00 per barrel, down 50 cents from Wednesday.
"We haven't found the bottom yet...we have been offering and offering but nobody wants to buy," a major said.
Regional demand remained mute with only Taiwan's 95-octane refomate tender for May/June closing next week on April 21.
Naphtha also fell with crude amid lack of fundamental support. Weak demand for prompt cargoes depressed May barrels to June levels with both swaps discussed at $21.00/$21.10 per barrel.
